text:
Yegor Sharangovich is one of the Flames' more reliable middle-six forwards, and his season is better than his seven points in 18 games suggest. Calgary has outshot opponents with him on the ice at five on five (56% of the shot attempts, 51% of the expected goals), which on a team that is usually outplayed counts for something. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he gets the puck out cleanly, 71% of his exits with possession, which keeps his line out of its own end.

The scoring should pick up. He's at 4.25 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and has three, and his teammates have shot cold with him on the ice too. Seven straight games without a point in late October was the low; since then he's scored in Seattle and set up two in Sunday's overtime win over Philadelphia. Evolving-Hockey had him barely above replacement last season (0.1 wins), so the ceiling isn't high, but our range has him around 17 goals by season's end, which is what Calgary needs from him.
